note: Both Image and GIF slots currently show the same still placeholder PNG. Reader caption and visibly labeled capture instructions are present under every planned slot.

slots.alt: Prune controls beside Unreal's native Actor Details filter row
slots.caption: Prune extends the existing Actor Details filter bar, keeping custom views alongside Unreal's normal filters.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture an Unreal Editor Details panel for a complex Actor with several native filters, two clearly named custom Prune filters, and all three Prune controls visible. Keep the Actor name and some expanded categories in frame.

slots.alt: Diagram of Prune's native Details panel extension points
slots.caption: Prune adds filter authoring and presentation controls around the native Details layout.
slots.capture_instructions: Create a labeled diagram showing the Unreal Property Editor, OnExtendActorDetails, FPruneModule, FPruneState and the native filter row. Show that Prune changes presentation rather than Actor data.

slots.alt: Prune plugin installed under an Unreal project's Plugins directory
slots.caption: A project-local installation keeps the plugin descriptor directly inside the Prune folder.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture Windows File Explorer at YourProject/Plugins/Prune, showing Prune.uplugin plus Source and Resources. Keep the address bar visible and avoid an extra nested Prune folder.

slots.alt: Creating and activating a custom Prune filter
slots.caption: A named filter reduces a complex Actor's Details panel to the categories needed for the current task.
slots.capture_instructions: Record a 10–15 second Unreal Editor animation: select a complex Actor, click +, name the filter Gameplay, uncheck two categories, reorder one, Save, and click Gameplay to show the simplified Details panel. End briefly on All.

slots.alt: Prune's New Filter window showing name, description and category choices
slots.caption: A custom filter combines its workflow name, scope and visible Details categories in one editor dialog.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture the New Filter dialog with Gameplay entered as the name, a realistic description, Class selected and several category checkboxes visible. Keep Save and Cancel in frame.

slots.alt: Category checkboxes and category search in the Prune filter editor
slots.caption: Prune lets each filter include the relevant Details categories while leaving unrelated property data intact.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture the filter editor with at least eight category names, several checked and unchecked rows, and a search query narrowing the visible choices. Keep a representative row's checkbox and category label readable.

slots.alt: Reordering categories in Prune's filter editor
slots.caption: Each filter can present the same Actor categories in a different order that suits its workflow.
slots.capture_instructions: Record a GIF showing at least eight filter-editor categories, dragging Gameplay above Rendering, the blue insertion line, Save, and the resulting Details panel category order. Keep the dragged category visible throughout.

slots.alt: Prune Class versus Global scope option
slots.caption: Class filters serve an Actor family; Global filters expose reusable views across Actor classes.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture the filter editor with Class/Global scope clearly visible and an Actor class label or tooltip. If possible include two side-by-side views showing the same Global filter available for different Actor types.

slots.alt: Editing and duplicating a Prune filter
slots.caption: Prune lets users adjust existing filters or create independent variants without changing Actor properties.
slots.capture_instructions: Record activating a single Gameplay filter, clicking Edit, changing one category, saving, then using Duplicate to create Gameplay Copy. Show both buttons in the native Details filter row at the end.

slots.alt: Editing and resetting an Epic Details filter
slots.caption: Prune can customize a built-in Epic filter and later return it to Unreal’s original definition.
slots.capture_instructions: Record selecting a native Rendering filter, opening Edit, hiding an unrelated category, saving, then using Reset to Epic Default. Show the category differences before and after reset.

slots.alt: Prune Filter Manager showing different filter types and actions
slots.caption: The manager combines custom presets, Epic filters and overrides in a searchable list.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture Filter Manager populated with an Epic filter, Epic Override, Prune Class and Prune Global filter. Show descriptions, active selection, visible-category counts, and the New, Import, Export, Reset Button Order and Done controls.

slots.alt: Prune's native filter row with controls and contextual actions
slots.caption: Filter buttons remain native Unreal controls while Prune adds authoring shortcuts and context menus.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture a close-up of the Actor Details filter row showing All, at least two Epic filters, two Prune filters and +, Manager, Edit icons. Open one Prune filter's right-click menu with its available actions legible.

slots.alt: Reordering filter buttons from the Prune Filter Manager
slots.caption: The Filter Manager can move favorite filter buttons ahead of less-used native filters.
slots.capture_instructions: Record dragging a Gameplay filter row above General in Filter Manager, closing the manager, then showing the reordered native filter buttons. Include Reset Button Order if it fits within a short sequence.

slots.alt: Exporting and importing a Prune filter preset
slots.caption: Portable JSON exports let the same filter layout be reused in another project or Actor class.
slots.capture_instructions: Record exporting a Gameplay filter from Filter Manager, then selecting another Actor class and importing the saved .prunefilters.json file. Show the imported filter appearing with a safe copy name if a collision occurs.

slots.alt: Prune plugin preferences in Unreal Project Settings
slots.caption: Appearance and default window sizes can be customized without changing any Actor properties.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture Project Settings → Plugins → Prune with Filter Editor Reordering, Filter Editor Window, Filter Bar, and Filter Manager Window groups expanded. Show default numeric values and the tooltip setting.

slots.alt: Diagram of Prune config storage and Actor property data
slots.caption: Prune stores filter definitions in editor-user configuration, separately from the Actors being inspected.
slots.capture_instructions: Create a three-part diagram: Prune editor-user config containing presets/overrides/order, the native Details filter row reading that config, and Actor/Component properties remaining untouched. Include a `.prunefilters.json` export as a separate portable file.

slots.alt: Diagram of Prune's source modules and Unreal Details integration
slots.caption: Prune’s module, state controller and Slate customization cooperate with Unreal’s native Property Editor.
slots.capture_instructions: Draw a technical diagram showing FPruneModule binding OnExtendActorDetails, FPruneDetailsCustomization building controls, FPruneState managing definitions, FPruneLayoutContext observing final category groups, and GEditorPerProjectIni storing filters.

slots.alt: Comparing a filtered Details panel against All
slots.caption: Switching to All is a reliable first check when a property appears missing from an active Prune filter.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture the same Actor with a custom filter active in one view and All in another, showing that a hidden category becomes visible again. Include the active filter labels.

slots.alt: Installed Prune plugin folder before replacing a release
slots.caption: Replacing the complete plugin folder avoids mixing source files and binaries from different releases.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture the Windows project Plugins/Prune folder with Prune.uplugin visible and the matching release ZIP shown nearby. Avoid showing personal usernames or proprietary project content.
